messages:
maria.chen: Heads-up: we received a DSAR today referencing an email in the legacy SFTP archive (bucket `legacy-retention`). Requester wants full erase + proof of deletion for redacted@example.com
jamal: That archive is still encrypted with `rw-legacy-key-v1` AFAIK. We rotated wrappers last year so need to check decrypt capability before we touch anything.
eli: Confirmed last rotation kept the primary key material in KMS but removed direct user bindings. Decrypt is possible via a service account grant. We must avoid broadening key access.
security-bot: ALERT: retention-exception candidate created (#SE-9421). Do not change key policies until approval.
ops-tom: I can provision a timebound IAM grant to service-account:sftp-erasure@infra with Decrypter role for 3 hours. Anyone object to 3h?
maria.chen: 3 hours ok. Legal: what evidence do we need to close the DSAR?
legal-sara: Need (1) deletion manifest linking the object(s) to the requester identifier, (2) auditable logs showing who executed the job and when, (3) confirmation of snapshot/backups handling. Prefer JSON manifest + KMS audit entries attached to the ticket.
jamal: On backups: we have tar snapshots under `sftp-archive/snapshots/YYYYMMDD.tar.gz`. Deleting files from live archive won't remove older tar snapshots. Options: a) redact and re-upload sanitized snapshots, b) rotate key and show inability to decrypt older snapshots (requires docs), or c) targeted rewrite of affected snapshots. Which does Legal prefer?
legal-sara: Prefer targeted redact when feasible. If doing key-rotation-as-inaccessibility, we need a signed internal attestation explaining process and scope.
eli: Ops proposal: 1) request 3h grant, 2) run safe-delete script that lists objects matching the identifier, verifies hashes, deletes, and emits line-delimited JSON proof for each object (example line: {"object":"sftp-archive/users/redacted@example.com/msg1.txt","action":"delete","by":"service-account:sftp-erasure@infra","ts":"2026-03-21T15:04:12Z"}), 3) gather KMS decrypt logs for the deletion run, 4) file a retention-exception for snapshot redaction/rewrite if needed.
ops-tom: Grant command used internally: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding rw-legacy-key-v1 --member=serviceAccount:sftp-erasure@infra --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter --condition='request.time < "2026-03-21T18:00:00Z"'`
jamal: Important: do NOT add broad roles like cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter. Minimal scope only. After delete, rotate any customer-facing wrappers and re-evaluate key policy.
maria.chen: I'll open the retention-exception doc for snapshot handling and add Legal to reviewer. Tom, please attach the JSON manifest + KMS log snippets to SE-9421 after the job.
ops-tom: Running dry-run now (list-only). Output sample: `{"object":"sftp-archive/users/redacted@example.com/msg1.txt","found_in":"snapshots/20210302.tar.gz","action":"dry-run-list"}`
eli: After dry-run, we'll run actual delete and then re-run snapshot inventory to identify snapshots needing redact.
security-bot: NOTE: KMS audit logs retention = 2 years. If Legal needs longer evidence retention, submit a retention-exception request.
legal-sara: 2 years sufficient for this DSAR. For snapshot redaction timeline, we'll accept a signed attestation + artifacts within 30 days.
maria.chen: OK, plan agreed. Assigning tasks: ops-tom -> run delete & upload artifacts; eli -> collect KMS logs & produce attest; me -> file retention-exception draft & coordinate with Legal. Close loop here. :thumbsup:
ops-tom: Delete complete at 2026-03-21T15:22Z. Pushing manifest and logs to ticket SE-9421. Sample manifest line included.
eli: Attached KMS decrypt audit snippets and operation summary to SE-9421.
legal-sara: Drafted confirmation template and signed statement ready pending the artifacts — will sign once manifest + logs are attached.
maria.chen: Thanks all. Reminder: keep change minimal, no permanent key policy changes in the process. We'll log the RBAC exception and revert grant at expiry.
